title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page does not belong to the motivic material on the neighbouring pages. The previous and next pages are manuscript notes on 'catégories de Demazure/Dennis', i.e. A-linear pseudo-abelian categories equivalent to categories of finitely generated projective modules over an algebra O. This page is instead page '- 48 -' of a typed analysis course in the Bourbaki/Dieudonné–Cartan style ('route', 'polycylindre', K = R or C, 'domaine').

The mathematics:
(1) End of the proof of a proposition. A closed holomorphic 1-form ω = Σ f_k dx_k on a domain A ⊂ K^n with the right topology (contractible / simply connected) has a holomorphic primitive. Earlier on the page's source, path-independence of ∫_γ ω follows from homotopy invariance (th.1), since ω is locally exact. Fix a base point a and set g(z) = ∫_γ ω along any route γ from a to z. For z_0 ∈ A, local exactness gives a polycylinder P centred at z_0 and a holomorphic u on P with du = ω and u(z_0) = g(z_0). Integrating along the segment σ: t ↦ z_0 + t(z − z_0) gives u(z) − u(z_0) = ∫_σ ω = g(z) − g(z_0). So g = u on P, hence g is holomorphic with dg = ω.
(2) Corollary for n = 1. Every holomorphic f on a contractible domain A ⊂ K has a primitive g with g' = f. Two primitives differ by a locally constant function, hence by a constant, since A is connected.
(3) Start of a 'variante'. Th.1 and prop.2 can be derived from a general principle of analytic continuation. At each z ∈ A one is given a family Φ(z) of open polycylinders centred at z and contained in A, and for each P ∈ Φ(z) a holomorphic u_P on P. Hypotheses so far: (i) for x ∈ P ∈ Φ(z) there is Q ∈ Φ(x) with u_Q(x) = u_P(x); (ii) if P ∩ Q ≠ ∅ and u_P, u_Q agree at one point of P ∩ Q, they agree on all of P ∩ Q (an identity-theorem-type condition). The statement breaks off ('enfin, si …'). It is clearly heading toward a monodromy theorem: on a simply connected domain such a compatible system glues to a global holomorphic function. This is the classical sheaf-of-germs / étalé-space form of the monodromy principle.
errors: No mathematical errors. 'Contractile' is a stronger hypothesis than needed; simple connectivity suffices.

The page appears misfiled. It is a typescript of an elementary analysis text, unrelated to the Galois theory of motives in the surrounding manuscript notes. It may be scrap paper whose blank verso Grothendieck used for the motive notes.

ideas.what: Existence of a holomorphic primitive of a closed holomorphic 1-form on a simply connected / contractible domain, via path integrals and local exactness on polycylinders
ideas.modern_name: Poincaré lemma / primitive on simply connected domains; homotopy invariance of line integrals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Cauchy, Riemann, Poincaré); textbook form in Cartan and Dieudonné
ideas.where_published: Standard textbooks, e.g. H. Cartan, Théorie élémentaire des fonctions analytiques; Dieudonné, Foundations of Modern Analysis

ideas.what: Analytic continuation principle stated through families of centred polycylinders with compatible holomorphic functions
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy theorem for a sheaf of holomorphic germs (local systems on simply connected spaces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass and Riemann; modern formulation by Cartan and others

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard textbook typescript page on primitives and analytic continuation, apparently not by Grothendieck and unrelated to the motivic notes around it. Nothing on it is new.
transcription_corrections: The struck-through '[-xxxx-]' is a typed overstrike 'xxxxx' cancelling a broken word at the line end. Nothing is lost.
'u_P(x)=u_Q(x)' near the bottom is typed faintly (appears as u_r / u_c) but means u_P, u_Q.
